title: A map of the mathematics

data.source: The results files of this library, read when the check is run (2026). No theorem of its own.

prediction: None. This book gathers the one-line status of every mathematics-shelf room and every theorem room, grouped by what CRR compares to. It tests nothing.
baseline: The rooms themselves: their results files as they stood when this check was last run (2026).
status_line: CRR here is: not tested; this book is the index of the others.
why: An index tests nothing, so no verdict about CRR is possible. Of 55 rooms gathered, 32 restate known mathematics, 6 fail, 8 are partly, 9 are untestable and 0 fit.

map.title: The far side, from the inside
map.line: a renaming of the cut locus of a circle taken by itself; a classical circle of distributions can always be shortcut through the larger space.

map.title: One number and a list of turnings
map.line: a renaming of reparametrisation invariance and Chentsov's theorem: one number for the circle and a list of turnings for the path.

map.title: Three gaps and a missed crossing
map.line: a renaming of the three-gap theorem for sampled rotations; a sampled monotone occasion shows a surplus of twice the overshoot.

map.title: The ringing beside the step
map.line: a renaming of the Wilbraham-Gibbs overshoot, which belongs to the filter and not to the cut.

map.title: The bus that is always late
map.line: a renaming of renewal theory (the inspection paradox); the gaps need not be independent.

map.title: The soup that is never finished
map.line: a renaming of simple exponential smoothing (Brown), with nothing left over.

map.title: The snail and the string
map.line: a renaming of the record (ladder) process of the lifted path; the count is not the winding number.

map.title: The swing with the shortening rope
map.line: a renaming of the adiabatic invariant, once coordinates are chosen, which R1 leaves open.

map.title: The only fair ruler, and how far apart two worlds can be
map.line: a renaming of Chentsov's unique metric; the theorems give no circle, no cut and no ruler size.

map.title: How many places can you tell apart?
map.line: a renaming of Wootters' statistical distance, if the ruler is a Cramer-Rao width; the number of looks is left free.

map.title: The wagon wheel that runs backwards
map.line: a renaming of the sampling theorem's half-turn condition (Itoh), with nothing left over.

map.title: The shrinking map
map.line: a renaming of a contraction map with rate q (Banach), with memory as a geometric series; on a circle the theorem's condition fails at the far point, as R5 already warns.

map.title: The spiral car park
map.line: a renaming of the lift of a path to the covering line; the cut rule then uses only differences and the line's direction, so it does not see the circle's own symmetry.

map.title: The tie at the far side
map.line: a renaming of the cut point of a circle (a tie between two equally short ways round); Morse theory finds no instability there, unlike the antipode of a sphere.

map.title: The meter that never looks at the gate
map.line: a renaming of the renewal-reward ratio; and the long-run surplus per unit time does not depend on where the cuts fall.

map.title: Which way is forwards?
map.line: a renaming of an arrow counted in loops; the fluctuation theorems derive the arrow and its exceptions, where R2 puts it in by hand.

map.title: What cannot be done
map.line: a renaming of a possible-or-impossible task statement (R6), with a number that constructor theory does not supply.

map.title: Immortal, but ever fainter
map.line: a renaming of Whitehead's inheritance from finished occasions, with a number for the fading.

map.title: Carrying soup across a sticky floor
map.line: a renaming of thermodynamic length, with a weaker bound than Salamon and Berry's.

map.title: Achilles and the rotor
map.line: a special case of the dwell-time cure for Zeno behaviour in hybrid systems; the finiteness is put in by the bounds.

map.title: The roundabout and the metronome
map.line: a special case of circle-map theory (Arnold's mode locking, Shapiro steps).

map.title: Why big clocks keep better time
map.line: a special case of the central limit theorem (independent gaps only); with correlated gaps the textbook correction is needed.

map.title: The wheel and the ruler
map.line: a special case of first-passage theory (the inverse Gaussian law); a fixed spread of 1/(2 pi) can hold at one noise level only.

map.title: How long is a wandering path?
map.line: a special case of Richardson's divider law: coherence is a true length only below the path's own correlation length.

map.title: Three ways to average a bag of odds
map.line: a special case of Amari's two flat means once a coordinate is chosen, which R5 does not do; its literal Frechet seed is neither projection but the known Karcher mean.

map.title: The odds of an early bell
map.line: a special case of large-deviation theory (R4's bounds are its zero-noise limit and R6's bound is its exponent); the odds of an early or late cut come from the theorem, not from CRR.

map.title: How hard to lean on the old seed
map.line: a special case of shrinkage estimation with the amount left free; Stein's theory sets q from the data, and 0.618 is the best pull only when the scatter of true contents is 0.618 of the noise.

map.title: The toll at the gate
map.line: a special case of Wald's identities (the mean wait and the mean surplus); the arithmetic S = 2B/sigma needs no theorem, and the cut is one edge of Wald's two-edged test.

map.title: Does the order of the post matter?
map.line: a special case of causal invariance, satisfied only trivially; a shared seed's forgetting is what breaks it.

map.title: The thick present
map.line: a special case of the precision-weighted (Kalman, free energy) update with the gain held fixed; the cut is CRR's own.

map.title: The wire that comes back late
map.line: a special case of a traced (feedback) process in category theory; the diagram does not see the ruler or the half-turn.

map.title: How fast can a thing become something else?
map.line: a special case of the Mandelstam-Tamm time (evenly weighted qubit paths only); elsewhere the cut is not the orthogonalisation time.

map.title: The ribbon that comes back inside out
map.line: a special case of Pancharatnam's phase jump (great-circle loops only); the count does not know the phase.

map.title: The linear twin
map.line: the same as an enduring hidden state at second order, exactly so only for Gaussian noise; with first-passage gaps the simple twin fails at third order.

map.title: Mass carries
map.line: silent. With mass the momentum crosses every cut, by the standard Markov property of a damped particle, and in the flat rotor mass is the same thing as a lasting force.

map.title: The ball that never stops bouncing
map.line: an assumption the standard result does not need (no pile-up of cuts follows from a fixed cut distance and no blow-up, not from tau > A); otherwise a special case of hybrid-systems theory.

map.title: The night watchman's round
map.line: in conflict with Kac's lemma as the wider notes word it (the wrong set, 180 times off); the cut rate itself is a renaming of the lemma.

map.title: Where is the middle of a ring of birds?
map.line: in conflict with the Kuramoto phase, if the Frechet mean is taken for it (a claim that room posed; Phoenix does not make it).

map.title: Four honest homes of the golden ratio
map.line: in conflict with the Kalman-Muth optimum only if 0.618 is called best (the theorem gives a seed weight of 0.382 at equal noise); R5's own 'no universal q' is what the theorems say.

map.title: The ball that waits for a lucky kick
map.line: in conflict with Kramers' escape theory as the old Omega dial (retired in Phoenix); below the critical push a cut is a Kramers escape.

map.title: What a steady tick costs
map.line: in conflict with the thermodynamic uncertainty relation, if a fixed spread of cut times is claimed (wider notes); R1 to R6 say nothing about regularity.

map.title: What crosses the cut
map.line: a Markov renewal process whose state at a cut is three things (which cut point, the force, the seed); the reading "only the seed crosses" fails whenever a force is running.

map.title: Ink in water
map.line: saying something de Bruijn's identity does not (an arc along a path of distributions); the two agree up to sqrt(2) for one bell curve being blurred, and on CRR's own carrier entropy does not move at all.

map.title: The turnstile and the tip
map.line: saying something the plain work theorem does not cover (W_cut is a switch triggered by a reading, so Jarzynski's equality does not apply); its heat Q, over kT, is a renaming of the fluctuation theorem's log odds for whole turns.

map.title: Who makes the maker?
map.line: saying less than closure to efficient causation: only the seed is rebuilt from inside, the other makers are not.

map.title: How hard was it to make?
map.line: silent where assembly theory speaks: R1 to R6 do not say which measure is the amount of history.

map.title: Who decides what happened first?
map.line: silent where causal-set growth speaks: CRR has clocks and no growth law between loops.

map.title: Does the loop hold together?
map.line: silent where integrated information theory speaks: R1 to R6 have no term for experience.

map.title: A fact for whom?
map.line: silent where relational quantum mechanics speaks: R1 to R6 are classical and make only the order of cuts relative.

map.title: How wide is now?
map.line: silent where the specious present speaks: R1 to R6 have no term for experience.

map.title: Four ways to keep a diary
map.line: silent where the four views of time differ: every observable is shared by all four.

map.title: What CRR says
map.line: not a comparison: the six statements themselves, shown on a toy clock.

map.title: The worm stays cut
map.line: not a comparison: a museum variant (wiping the seed) that loses to plain R5, which is the Kalman recursion.

map.title: The garden of forking paths
map.line: not a comparison: a count of how many fair mappings would have passed the seed bet.

map.title: Where CRR stands
map.line: not a comparison: a table that places CRR among other frameworks, by judgement.

lead.unneeded assumption: an assumption the known result does not need:
lead.different: saying something the known result does not:
lead.silent: silent where the known result speaks:
